title: Terminal widget SDK: user-authored, hot-loaded widget apps with a grid layout engine and ambient zones
contract: 8 entries (§6): a widget app contract (own state, input reducer, render, composing the same layout/theme primitives the built-ins use), a modal widget slot that owns every keystroke while open, ambient dock/float zones, a CSS-grid-like terminal layout engine with fr tracks and named areas, demo apps (/grid-test, /dialog-test, /ticker, /weather), and **user widget apps loaded from `$HERMES_HOME/tui-widgets/*.mjs`, hot-reloaded without a restart** — explicitly so that Hermes itself can author new widgets at runtime.
governance: Would perform a privileged effect (arbitrary code execution in the client). If ever revisited, loading a widget must cross `skill.install` with the same digest + owner-approval floor as any other acquired capability.
historical_exclusion_reason: A hot-loaded `.mjs` file that the agent may author and that runs unsandboxed inside the client process is the exact code-execution seam Nerva's skill importer exists to close: digest verification, owner approval, recorded provenance, and a `skill.install` kernel crossing that even a kernel GRANT cannot bypass. Shipping a parallel widget loader would reopen it under the cover of 'it's only UI', which is worse than reopening it honestly. This is the clearest case in the cluster where copying a working feature would be a governance regression. Re-open path: only as a *rendering* format — declarative widget descriptions the hub emits and the client draws, with no executable code crossing the boundary.
